title: File BL-28: every caption is stored three times, and approve it
body:
Files **BL-28** and records the owner's approval of it.

**Measured across the whole cached corpus, not estimated.** 285 of 285 transcripts carry roughly three copies of every spoken word:

| | characters |
| --- | --- |
| stored in `data/transcripts/` | 38,767,230 |
| actual speech | 13,645,734 |
| **ratio** | **2.84x** |

2.54x to 3.00x per video, median 2.96x. **Not one video escapes it.**

**The mechanism.** YouTube's automatic captions use a **roll-up** presentation — two lines scroll on screen, and the track emits a cue for every *display frame* rather than for every line of speech. Every line appears three times: alone, as the tail of the previous frame, as the head of the next. Of 4,430 cues in one video, 50% extend the previous cue, 49% are a suffix of it, and 50% start within 0.02s of it. The structure is exact.

`parse_vtt` is not defective. It keeps every cue, which is correct for an ordinary WebVTT and wrong for a roll-up one.

**Why no gate saw it.** `tests/fixtures/captions_vtt.txt` — the only WebVTT the suite has ever parsed — has clean, non-overlapping cues. YouTube has never sent this project captions shaped like that fixture. That is **ESC-21 repeating exactly**: the fixture agreed with the code and both disagreed with what yt-dlp returns.

**Confirmed against the source, not argued.** The same caption track fetched in both offered formats:

| | characters | words |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `vtt`, as stored today | 217,427 | 40,966 |
| `json3`, every segment concatenated | 73,159 | 13,791 |

Four videos checked, all 2.97x–3.00x, all offering `json3`.

**The second cost is not money.** R5 cuts every excerpt window from a mention's `start_seconds`, and V11/V14 make that timestamp the thing the owner acts on. In roll-up VTT a board name inside a two-line frame inherits the **first** line's timestamp — up to ~2.5 seconds early. `json3` carries per-word offsets on 72% of segments, so the timestamp lands on the word.

**Direction, the owner's, agreed after reviewing the comparison:** prefer `json3`; keep VTT as a fallback with de-duplication; and **the fallback must announce itself loudly**, per video and in the summary, so two provenance classes never sit in one cache with nothing to tell them apart. `json3` is undocumented and can change, which is exactly why the VTT path stays rather than being deleted.

One correction worth carrying forward: `aAppend` events must be **kept**. They hold real speech — dropping them loses 2,257 words on the measured video. The roll-up structure lives in `wWinId`/`wpWinPosId`, not in the text.

The VTT reconstruction was validated against `json3` as ground truth and lands within **0.05%**, which is what makes it sound as a fallback rather than a guess.

Evidence and approval only. No code, no design amendment — the decision and the plan follow on their own pull requests, in that order.
